title: After finding out details about a stranger, we mistakenly th…

sents.en: After finding out details about a stranger, we mistakenly think that they also know about us.
sents.cn: 在了解一个陌生人的详情后，我们会错误地认为他们也了解我们。

sents.en: As a result, we act more honestly around them, according to a recent study in Nature.
sents.cn: 其结果便是，我们在他们面前表现得更诚实，这是《自然》期刊最近一项研究的发现。

sents.en: Past research has found that we tend to assume social relationships are reciprocal (相互 的).
sents.cn: 过去的研究发现，我们往往假设社会关系是相互的（相互的）。

sents.en: Most of the time, this assumption is accurate: someone you think of as a friend will usually consider you a friend too.
sents.cn: 大多数时候，这一假设是准确的：你视为朋友的人通常也会把你当朋友。

sents.en: But sometimes our social ties are more one-sided: for example, you might learn something about a stranger who doesn't know you at all.
sents.cn: 但有时我们的社会联系更偏向单方面：例如，你可能对一个完全不认识你的陌生人有所了解。

sents.en: Researchers Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest wondered whether our tendency to believe that social ties are reciprocal could lead us to mistakenly feel that a stranger does actually know us.
sents.cn: 研究人员阿努杰∙沙阿和迈克尔∙拉福雷斯特想知道，我们相信社会关系相互的倾向，是否会导致我们错误地感觉某个陌生人确实认识我们。

sents.en: In a series of lab-based studies, this is exactly what the researchers found.
sents.cn: 在一系列基于实验室的研究中，研究人员恰恰发现了这一点。

sents.en: When we know about strangers, we erroneously think they also know about us.
sents.cn: 当我们了解陌生人时，会错误地认为他们也了解我们。

sents.en: But the really interesting finding came when the researchers stepped out of the lab, to conduct a field experiment.
sents.cn: 但真正有趣的发现出现在研究人员走出实验室、进行实地实验时。

sents.en: The team developed leaflets (传单) containing fairly ordinary information about local community police officers, such as their favourite food, hobbies, or reasons for joining the police force.
sents.cn: 团队制作了传单（传单），内容包含关于当地社区警察相当普通的信息，比如他们最喜欢的食物、爱好，或加入警队的原因。

sents.en: They then sent out these leaflets to every apartment in a number of housing developments in disadvantaged areas.
sents.cn: 随后他们将这些传单发送到多个弱势地区住宅区中的每一套公寓。

sents.en: The officers themselves also dropped off cards to local residents containing similar information.
sents.cn: 警察本人也向当地居民投放了含有类似信息的卡片。

sents.en: Two months later, the researchers surveyed residents at these housing developments as well as control areas that did not receive leaflets or outreach cards.
sents.cn: 两个月后，研究人员调查了这些住宅区的居民，以及未收到传单或外联卡片的对照地区居民。

sents.en: Residents were asked to imagine that they had committed a crime and how likely it would be that local officers would find out about it.
sents.cn: 居民被要求想象自己犯了罪，以及当地警察发现此事的可能性有多大。

sents.en: They also rated how well the officers in the area knew them.
sents.cn: 他们还评估了该地区的警察对他们的了解程度

sents.en: The team found that residents of the developments that had received the leaflets believed it more likely that local officers would find out about illegal activity than residents of the control areas.
sents.cn: 团队发现，收到传单的住宅区居民比对照地区的居民更倾向于相信，当地警察会发现非法活动。

sents.en: Even more strikingly, the team found that immediately after the leaflet distribution, there were fewer criminal complaints and arrests in the areas around the developments that had received the leaflets than around the control developments.
sents.cn: 更引人注目的是，团队发现就在传单发放后，收到传单的住宅区周边地区的犯罪投诉和逮捕数量，少于对照住宅区周边地区。
